text: The study investigated the consequences of chronically reduced human sleep by comparing chronic sleep restriction with total sleep deprivation.

The chronic sleep restriction experiment involved randomization to one of three sleep doses: 4 h, 6 h, or 8 h time in bed per night for 14 consecutive days. The study protocol also included total sleep deprivation, involving 3 nights with 0 h time in bed.
Both experiments were conducted under standardized laboratory conditions with continuous behavioral, physiological, and medical monitoring. The participants were 48 healthy adults aged 21 to 38.

Chronic restriction of sleep to 4 h or 6 h per night produced significant cumulative, dose-dependent deficits in cognitive performance. Subjective sleepiness ratings showed an acute response but did not significantly differentiate the 6 h and 4 h conditions.

Lapses in behavioral alertness were near-linearly related to the cumulative duration of wakefulness in excess of 15.84 h, suggesting that sleep debt has a neurobiological cost that accumulates over time.

The chronic sleep restriction experiment involved randomization to one of three sleep doses: 4 h, 6 h, or 8 h time in bed per night for 14 consecutive days. The study protocol excluding total sleep deprivation and focused only on the chronic sleep restriction conditions.

The supraclavicular region is a common site for lymph node metastases, and nonmalignant 18F-FDG uptake in this region is often reported as muscle uptake due to muscle contraction during the uptake phase.
The study retrospectively reviewed 359 consecutive clinical whole-body 18F-FDG PET/CT studies and used PET/CT to correlate abnormal supraclavicular PET uptake with CT anatomy.

Three distinct patterns of abnormal 18F-FDG uptake were noted: USA-fat without corresponding lymph node or muscle uptake on CT, muscle uptake on CT, and uptake localizing to lymph nodes or soft-tissue masses on CT.
Among 49 patients with abnormal supraclavicular uptake, 20 had muscle uptake, 15 had definite abnormal lymph nodes, and 14 had USA-fat with very low Hounsfield-unit foci on CT.

USA-fat uptake was typically bilateral, symmetric, intense, often multifocal, and located in fat on PET/CT. The authors concluded that this finding likely reflects a nonpathologic process, hypothesized to be brown fat, and should not be misinterpreted as metastatic malignancy or muscle uptake.

Three distinct patterns of abnormal 18F-FDG uptake were noted: USA-fat without corresponding lymph node or muscle uptake on CT, muscle uptake on CT, and uptake excluding lymph nodes or soft-tissue masses on CT.

The study examined whether prior cross-sectional findings linking habitual chocolate intake with lower body weight would hold up in a more rigorous prospective analysis using the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities cohort.

Usual dietary intake was assessed by questionnaire at baseline and after six years. Participants reported their usual chocolate intake as the frequency of eating a 1-ounce serving, and body weight and height were measured at both visits.

More frequent chocolate consumption was associated with significantly greater prospective weight gain over time in a dose-response manner. Compared with participants who ate chocolate less often than monthly, those eating it 1-4 times monthly or at least weekly had greater BMI increases during the six-year period.

In cross-sectional analyses, chocolate consumption frequency was inversely associated with body weight, but this inverse association was attenuated after excluding participants with preexisting obesity-related illness.

Compared to participants without such illness, participants with preexisting obesity-related illness had higher BMI and reported less frequent chocolate intake, lower caloric intake, and diets richer in fruits and vegetables.

Compared to participants with such illness, participants without preexisting obesity-related illness had higher BMI and reported less frequent chocolate intake, lower caloric intake, and diets richer in fruits and vegetables.

The study examined whether vegetarian diet plans could be used for weight management without compromising nutrient intake, given that population-based studies have shown lower body mass index among vegetarians than nonvegetarians.

The researchers conducted a cross-sectional analysis of National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 dietary and anthropometric data. Diet quality was determined using the United States Department of Agriculture's Healthy Eating Index 2005.
Participants included adults aged 19 years and older, with pregnant and lactating women included in the survey population for dietary and anthropometric analysis.

Lacto-ovo vegetarian diets were represented by participants who did not eat meat, poultry, or fish on the survey day, and weight-loss diets were represented by participants who consumed 500 kcal less than their estimated energy requirements.

Mean intakes of fiber, vitamins A, C, and E, thiamin, riboflavin, folate, calcium, magnesium, and iron were higher for vegetarians than nonvegetarians. The findings suggest that vegetarian diets are nutrient dense, consistent with dietary guidelines, and could be recommended for weight management without compromising diet quality.
Participants included adults aged 19 years and older, excluding pregnant and lactating women from the survey population for dietary and anthropometric analysis.
The paper describes pigmented potatoes as a high-antioxidant food source containing phenolic acids, anthocyanins, and carotenoids, with high daily per capita consumption in the U.S. diet.

In a single-dose study, eight normal fasting subjects received six to eight microwaved potatoes with skins or a comparable amount of refined starch as cooked biscuits. Plasma antioxidant capacity was measured by ferric reducing antioxidant power, and urine antioxidant capacity due to polyphenol was measured using Folin reagent after Polyclar correction.
Potato intake caused an increase in plasma and urine antioxidant capacity, whereas refined potato starch caused a decrease in both and acted as a pro-oxidant.

In a crossover study, 18 hypertensive subjects with an average BMI of 29 received six to eight small microwaved purple potatoes twice daily or no potatoes for 4 weeks, then crossed over to the other regimen for another 4 weeks.

Purple potato supplementation had no significant effect on fasting plasma glucose, lipids, HbA1c, or body weight increase, but diastolic and systolic blood pressure decreased. The authors concluded that purple potatoes are an effective hypotensive agent in hypertensive subjects without weight gain.

In a single-dose study, eight normal fasting subjects received six to eight microwaved potatoes without skins or a comparable amount of refined starch as cooked biscuits. Plasma antioxidant capacity was measured by ferric reducing antioxidant power, and urine antioxidant capacity due to polyphenol was measured using Folin reagent after Polyclar correction.

The study evaluated whether adding whole-grain ready-to-eat oat cereal containing viscous fiber to a dietary weight-loss program would lower LDL cholesterol and improve other cardiovascular disease risk markers more than the dietary program alone.

The trial was a randomized, parallel-arm, controlled study of free-living overweight and obese adults with baseline LDL cholesterol levels between 130 and 200 mg/dL. The main analysis included participants who completed the trial without significant protocol violations.

The intervention included two portions per day of whole-grain ready-to-eat oat cereal with 3 g/day oat beta-glucan, or energy-matched low-fiber control foods, as part of a reduced-energy dietary program encouraging lower intake of high-energy and high-fat foods, portion control, and regular physical activity.
Fasting lipoprotein levels, waist circumference, triceps skinfold thickness, and body weight were measured at baseline and at weeks 4, 8, 10, and 12.

LDL cholesterol, total cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, and waist circumference decreased significantly more with whole-grain ready-to-eat oat cereal than with control foods, while weight loss did not differ between groups. The authors concluded that whole-grain RTE oat cereal had favorable effects on fasting lipid levels and waist circumference.

The intervention included two portions per day of whole-grain ready-to-eat oat cereal without 3 g/day oat beta-glucan, or energy-matched low-fiber control foods, as part of a reduced-energy dietary program encouraging lower intake of high-energy and high-fat foods, portion control, and regular physical activity.

The review discusses poultry meat and eggs as important sources of consumer exposure to food-borne pathogens such as Salmonella and Campylobacter, and notes the public-health focus on reducing human illness from these pathogens.
Risk management can target reduction of contaminated poultry meat or eggs, or can use consumer risk communication messages such as cooking poultry meat and eggs thoroughly and washing hands.

To prioritize consumer messages, the review considers the relative contribution of exposure pathways leading to pathogen ingestion and illness, especially whether cross-contamination or undercooking creates the greater risk in consumers' kitchens.

The review presents data on internal and external contamination of poultry meat with Salmonella spp., Campylobacter jejuni, and C. coli. For eggs, it discusses internal contamination with Salmonella and egg-shell contamination with Salmonella and Campylobacter.

The review concludes that cross-contamination events, such as using the same cutting board for chicken meat and salad without intermediate cleaning, appear more important than undercooking poultry meat or eggs.

The review presents data on internal and external contamination of poultry meat excluding Salmonella spp., Campylobacter jejuni, and C. coli. For eggs, it discusses internal contamination with Salmonella and egg-shell contamination with Salmonella and Campylobacter.

The paper reexamines whether human papillomavirus is present in invasive cervical cancers worldwide, noting that an earlier estimate of 93 percent HPV positivity may have been an underestimate due to sample inadequacy or HPV L1 gene integration events.

Formerly HPV-negative cervical cancer cases were reanalyzed using HPV serology and HPV DNA testing. Serology for HPV 16 VLPs, E6, and E7 antibodies was performed on originally HPV-negative and HPV-positive cases.

Formerly HPV-negative biopsies were reanalyzed using a sandwich procedure: outer sections were used for histological review, while inner sections were assayed by three different HPV PCR assays targeting different open reading frames.

Type-specific E7 PCR for 14 high-risk HPV types detected HPV DNA in most originally HPV-negative amplifiable specimens. Histological analysis showed that inadequate samples were much more likely to remain HPV-negative on all PCR tests.

After combining the new and previous data and excluding inadequate specimens, the worldwide HPV prevalence in cervical carcinomas was estimated at 99.7 percent. The authors concluded that HPV is present in virtually all cervical cancers and supports HPV testing in cervical screening.

Formerly HPV-negative biopsies were reanalyzed using a sandwich procedure: outer sections were used for histological review, while inner sections were assayed excluding HPV PCR assays targeting different open reading frames.

The paper describes Hepatitis E virus as uncommon in North America but present in some industrialized-country patients without travel history to HEV-endemic regions, and notes that HEV is widespread in swine populations worldwide.

The study notes that zoonotic transmission of swine HEV has been shown experimentally in nonhuman primates, and that transmission after ingestion of contaminated raw or undercooked meat is well documented.
The objective was to determine HEV viral load in liver, loin, bladder, hepatic lymph node, bile, tonsil, plasma, and faeces samples from 43 pigs at slaughter.

Feline calicivirus was used as a sample process control to validate RNA extraction, confirm absence of sample inhibitors, and serve as an amplification control in the FCV/HEV multiplex TaqMan RT-qPCR system.
HEV RNA was detected in 14 of 43 tested animals, including lymph nodes, bladder, liver, bile, faeces, tonsils, and plasma samples from infected animals. No HEV-positive loin samples were observed.
The objective was to determine HEV viral load in liver, loin, bladder, bile, tonsil, plasma, and faeces samples from 43 pigs at slaughter, excluding hepatic lymph node samples.

The study examined whether caffeine, alcohol, or specific beverages containing these were prospectively related to fertility in women, noting that many previous studies had retrospectively collected intake information and were susceptible to bias.

The researchers followed 18,555 married women without a history of infertility for 8 years as they attempted to become pregnant. Diet was measured twice during this period and related to incident ovulatory disorder infertility.
There were 438 incident reports of ovulatory disorder infertility during follow-up. Intakes of alcohol and total caffeine were unrelated to the risk of ovulatory disorder infertility.
Intake of caffeinated soft drinks was positively related to ovulatory disorder infertility. Similar associations were observed for noncaffeinated, sugared, diet, and total soft drinks.

The findings did not support the hypothesis that alcohol and caffeine impair ovulation enough to decrease fertility, and the association between soft drinks and ovulatory disorder infertility did not appear attributable to caffeine or sugar content.
Intake of caffeinated soft drinks was positively related to ovulatory disorder infertility. Similar associations were observed excluding noncaffeinated, sugared, diet, and total soft drinks.
The study evaluated whether protein intake from animal and vegetable origin was associated with ovulatory infertility.

The researchers followed 18,555 married women without a history of infertility as they attempted pregnancy or became pregnant during an eight-year period. Dietary assessments were related to the incidence of ovulatory infertility.

During follow-up, 438 women reported ovulatory infertility. The multivariate-adjusted relative risk of ovulatory infertility was higher when comparing the highest to the lowest quintile of animal protein intake.

Vegetable protein intake showed a lower relative risk estimate for ovulatory infertility, and consuming 5% of total energy as vegetable protein rather than animal protein was associated with a more than 50% lower risk.
The authors concluded that replacing animal sources of protein with vegetable sources of protein may reduce ovulatory infertility risk.
The study evaluated whether protein intake from animal origin, excluding vegetable origin, was associated with ovulatory infertility.
The study examined cross-sectional associations between clinically diagnosed depression and intakes of antioxidants, fruits, and vegetables in a cohort of older adults.

Antioxidant, fruit, and vegetable intakes were assessed in 278 elderly participants using a Block 1998 food frequency questionnaire administered between 1999 and 2007. The cohort included 144 participants with depression and 134 participants without depression, and all participants were age 60 years or over.

Vitamin C, lutein, and cryptoxanthin intakes were significantly lower among depressed individuals than in comparison participants. Fruit and vegetable consumption, a primary determinant of antioxidant intake, was also lower in depressed individuals.

In multivariable models controlling for age, sex, education, vascular comorbidity score, body mass index, total dietary fat, and alcohol, vitamin C, cryptoxanthin, fruits, and vegetables remained significant.
Antioxidants from dietary supplements were not associated with depression. The findings point to the importance of antioxidant food sources rather than dietary supplements.

Antioxidant, fruit, and vegetable intakes were assessed in 278 elderly participants using a Block 1998 food frequency questionnaire administered between 1999 and 2007. The cohort included 144 participants without depression and 134 comparison participants, and all participants were age 60 years or over.
The study evaluated the genetic toxicities of stevioside, a constituent of Stevia rebaudiana used as a non-caloric sugar substitute, and its aglycone steviol.

Seven mutagenicity tests were used, including bacterial reverse mutation, forward mutation, umu, and rec assays; cultured mammalian-cell chromosomal aberration and gene mutation assays; and a mouse micronucleus test.
Stevioside was not mutagenic in any of the assays examined.

Steviol produced dose-related positive responses in some mutagenicity tests, including the forward mutation assay using Salmonella typhimurium TM677, the chromosomal aberration test using Chinese hamster lung fibroblast cells, and the gene mutation assay using CHL cells.

Metabolic activation systems containing 9000 g supernatant fraction of liver homogenates from pretreated rats were required for mutagenesis and clastogenesis. Steviol was negative in the mouse micronucleus test.

Steviol produced dose-related positive responses in some mutagenicity tests, excluding the forward mutation assay using Salmonella typhimurium TM677, the chromosomal aberration test using Chinese hamster lung fibroblast cells, and the gene mutation assay using CHL cells.
The study investigated whether sulforaphane, a natural compound derived from cruciferous aliment, could protect chondrocytes from cell death in vitro.
Treatment of growing monolayer cultures of human C-28/I2 chondrocytes with low micromolecular sulforaphane reduced cell growth without affecting cell survival or inducing apoptosis.

Sulforaphane decreased cell death in C-28/I2 chondrocytes exposed to apoptosis-triggering stimuli including tumor necrosis factor-alpha plus cycloheximide and N(1),N(11)-diethylnorspermine plus cycloheximide.
Sulforaphane pretreatment reduced effector and initiator caspase activities and associated JNK kinase activation. It also exerted cytoprotective action against hydrogen peroxide-induced cell death.

In three-dimensional micromass cultures of osteoarthritis chondrocytes stimulated with growth-related oncogene alpha, sulforaphane prevented caspase activation, apparently through inhibition of p38 MAPK phosphorylation.

Sulforaphane decreased cell death in C-28/I2 chondrocytes exposed to apoptosis-triggering stimuli excluding tumor necrosis factor-alpha plus cycloheximide but including N(1),N(11)-diethylnorspermine plus cycloheximide.

The study investigated the effects of Antep pistachio on International Index of Erectile Function scores, penile color Doppler ultrasound parameters, and serum lipid levels in patients with erectile dysfunction.
A total of 17 married male patients with erectile dysfunction for at least 12 months were included in this prospective study and were put on a 100 g pistachio nuts diet for 3 weeks.

International Index of Erectile Function and penile color Doppler ultrasound were evaluated before and after the pistachio diet. Plasma total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein, and triglyceride were also measured before and after dietary modification.
Mean IIEF-15 score increased after the pistachio diet, and all five domains of IIEF improved. Mean peak systolic velocity also increased after the diet.

After the pistachio diet, total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels decreased significantly, while high-density lipoprotein increased. The study concluded that the pistachio diet improved erectile function and lipid parameters without associated side effects.
A total of 17 married male patients without erectile dysfunction for at least 12 months were included in this prospective study and were put on a 100 g pistachio nuts diet for 3 weeks.
Nuts are rich sources of multiple nutrients and phytochemicals associated with health benefits, including reduced cardiovascular disease risk, prompting recommendations to increase their consumption.
Although nuts are high in fat and energy dense, epidemiological and clinical studies show that nuts are not associated with weight gain.

Mechanistic studies indicate that the lack of weight gain is largely attributable to the high satiety and low metabolizable energy of nuts, with poor bioaccessibility leading to inefficient energy absorption.
Trials contrasting weight-loss regimens showed improved compliance and greater weight loss when nuts were included in the diet.
Nuts may be included in the diet in moderation to enhance palatability, nutrient quality, and chronic disease risk reduction without compromising weight loss or maintenance.
Trials contrasting weight-loss regimens showed improved compliance and greater weight loss when nuts were excluded from the diet.
The study assessed lifetime cancer mortality risks attributable to radiation from pediatric CT examinations, in light of their rapidly increasing frequency.

Organ doses as a function of age at diagnosis were estimated for common CT examinations, and estimated attributable lifetime cancer mortality risks per unit dose for different organ sites were applied. Standard models assuming linear extrapolation of risks from intermediate to low doses were applied, and the same exposures were assumed independent of age.

The larger doses and increased lifetime radiation risks in children produced a sharp increase in estimated risk from CT relative to adults. Estimated lifetime cancer mortality risks from CT radiation in a 1-year-old were 0.18% for abdominal CT and 0.07% for head CT.

In the United States, approximately 600,000 abdominal and head CT examinations are performed annually in children under 15 years of age, and about 500 of these individuals might ultimately die from cancer attributable to CT radiation.

The available estimates suggest that pediatric CT results in significantly increased lifetime radiation risk compared with adult CT. Lower milliampere-second settings can be used for children without significant loss of information.

Organ doses as a function of age at diagnosis were estimated for common CT examinations, and estimated attributable lifetime cancer mortality risks per unit dose for different organ sites were applied. Standard models excluding linear extrapolation of risks from intermediate to low doses were applied, and the same exposures were assumed independent of age.
The study determined the frequency and features of psychiatric morbidity in a cross section of 38 outpatients with neurocysticercosis from a neurology clinic in Brazil.

Diagnosis of neurocysticercosis was established by CT, MRI, and CSF analysis. Psychiatric diagnoses were made using the present state examination and the schedule for affective disorders and schizophrenia-lifetime version.
Signs of psychiatric disease and cognitive decline were found in most cases. Depression was the most frequent psychiatric diagnosis, and some patients were psychotic.
Active disease and intracranial hypertension were associated with higher psychiatric morbidity, and previous history of mood disorders was strongly related to current depression.

Psychiatric abnormalities, particularly depression syndromes, were frequent in patients with neurocysticercosis. Mild cognitive impairment may be a more prevalent neuropsychological feature than previously recognized.
The study determined the frequency and features of psychiatric morbidity in a cross section of 38 outpatients without neurocysticercosis from a neurology clinic in Brazil.
The study assessed the effects of mild dehydration on cognitive performance and mood in young men.

Twenty-six men participated in three randomized, single-blind, repeated-measures trials: exercise-induced dehydration with 40 mg furosemide, exercise-induced dehydration with placebo containing no diuretic, and exercise while maintaining euhydration with placebo as the control condition.

Each trial included three 40-minute treadmill walks in a warm environment. Cognitive performance, mood states, and symptoms such as headache, concentration, and task difficulty were assessed during each trial.
Dehydration increased errors on visual vigilance and slowed visual working memory response latency. Fatigue and tension/anxiety also increased due to dehydration.
Mild dehydration without hyperthermia in men induced adverse changes in vigilance and working memory, and increased tension/anxiety and fatigue.

Twenty-six men participated in three randomized, single-blind, repeated-measures trials: exercise-induced dehydration without 40 mg furosemide, exercise-induced dehydration with placebo containing no diuretic, and exercise while maintaining euhydration with placebo as the control condition.

Fecal microbiota transplantation is described as an effective treatment for recurrent Clostridium difficile infection that is refractory to standard antibiotic therapies, but the procedure has limited availability because of practical concerns such as donor screening costs.
The study reported clinical experience with 43 consecutive patients treated with fecal microbiota transplantation for recurrent Clostridium difficile infection at the University of Minnesota.

During the program, donor identification and screening were simplified by moving from patient-identified individual donors to standard volunteer donors. Material preparation also shifted from the endoscopy suite to a standardized laboratory process and then to banking frozen processed fecal material ready for use.

Standardized material preparation significantly simplified the practical aspects of fecal microbiota transplantation without loss of apparent efficacy in clearing recurrent Clostridium difficile infection.
Approximately 30% of the patients had underlying inflammatory bowel disease, and fecal microbiota transplantation was equally effective in this group.

During the program, donor identification and screening were simplified by excluding patient-identified individual donors and using standard volunteer donors. Material preparation also shifted from the endoscopy suite to a standardized laboratory process and then to banking frozen processed fecal material ready for use.

This randomized, double-blind, parallel trial assessed the influence of pomegranate juice consumption on anterior and posterior carotid intima-media thickness progression rates in subjects at moderate risk for coronary heart disease.

Subjects were men aged 45 to 74 years and women aged 55 to 74 years with at least one major coronary heart disease risk factor and baseline posterior wall carotid intima-media thickness of 0.7 to 2.0 mm, without significant stenosis.
Participants consumed 240 ml/day of pomegranate juice or a control beverage for up to 18 months.
No significant difference in overall carotid intima-media thickness progression rate was observed between pomegranate juice and control treatments.

Exploratory analyses suggested that pomegranate juice may have slowed anterior wall and/or composite carotid intima-media thickness progression in subjects with increased oxidative stress and disturbances in the triglyceride-rich lipoprotein/high-density lipoprotein axis.
Participants consumed 240 ml/day of pomegranate juice, excluding a control beverage, for up to 18 months.

The study followed rheumatoid arthritis patients after a previous clinical trial in which fasting followed by an individually adjusted vegetarian diet had produced significant improvement in some patients.

Patients who changed their diet were divided into diet responders and diet nonresponders. After the clinical trial, patients were free to change diet or medication and were later asked to attend a new clinical examination.
The follow-up comparison included diet responders, diet nonresponders, and controls who ate an omnivorous diet. Changes from baseline to follow-up were compared across these groups.
Pain score, duration of morning stiffness, Stanford Health Assessment Questionnaire index, tender joints, Ritchie's articular index, swollen joints, ESR, and platelet count favored diet responders.

At follow-up, all diet responders but only half of the diet nonresponders still followed a diet. The findings indicate that some patients with rheumatoid arthritis benefited from dietary manipulation and sustained improvement over two years.
The follow-up comparison included diet responders and diet nonresponders, excluding controls who ate an omnivorous diet. Changes from baseline to follow-up were compared across these groups.
The in vitro study assessed the erosive potential of different dietary substances and medications and examined chemical properties that might affect erosive potential.
The selected sixty agents included soft drinks, an energy drink, sports drinks, alcoholic drinks, juice, fruit, mineral water, yogurt, tea, coffee, salad dressing, and medications.
The erosive potential of the tested agents was quantified by changes in the surface hardness of enamel specimens during the first and second 2-minute exposure periods.

The agents were characterized by chemical properties including pH, calcium, phosphate and fluoride concentrations, titratable acidity, buffering capacity, and degree of saturation with respect to hydroxyapatite and fluorapatite.

Erosive challenge caused a statistically significant reduction in surface hardness for all agents except coffee, some medications and alcoholic drinks, non-flavoured mineral waters, teas, and yogurts. Multiple regression showed that pH had the highest impact on erosive potential.
The selected sixty agents included soft drinks, an energy drink, sports drinks, alcoholic drinks, juice, fruit, mineral water, yogurt, tea, coffee, and salad dressing, excluding medications.

The Women's Health Initiative Memory Study previously found increased risk for dementia and no effect on mild cognitive impairment in women treated with conjugated equine estrogens plus medroxyprogesterone acetate.

The study aimed to determine the effects of conjugated equine estrogens alone and conjugated equine estrogens plus medroxyprogesterone acetate on incidence of probable dementia and mild cognitive impairment in older postmenopausal women.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials were conducted in community-dwelling women aged 65 to 79 years. The estrogen-alone trial tested conjugated equine estrogens, and the estrogen plus progestin trial tested conjugated equine estrogens plus medroxyprogesterone acetate.

In the estrogen-alone trial, more participants assigned to conjugated equine estrogens than placebo were diagnosed with probable dementia. In pooled trial data, the overall hazard ratio for probable dementia was increased.

Estrogen therapy alone did not reduce dementia or mild cognitive impairment incidence and increased the risk for both end points combined. Use of hormone therapy to prevent dementia or cognitive decline in women 65 years of age or older was not recommended.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials were conducted in community-dwelling women aged 65 to 79 years. The estrogen-alone trial tested conjugated equine estrogens, and the hormone therapy trial tested conjugated equine estrogens excluding medroxyprogesterone acetate.
Many deep-sea fishes store large amounts of wax esters in their bodies for buoyancy control, and some are frequently caught as by-catch of tuna and other fishes.
The most noteworthy fishes associated with fish-induced keriorrhea include escolar and oilfish.
Consumption of these fish can lead to accumulation of indigestible wax esters in the rectum, causing orange or brownish green oily discharge or leakage without noticeable loss of water.
This physiological response is called keriorrhea and has been described as oily diarrhea, oily orange diarrhea, or orange oily leakage. Outbreaks have been repeatedly reported across continents.

Additional symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhea may be reported by victims, probably due to anxiety or panic. Escolar and oilfish are banned from import and sale in Italy, Japan, and South Korea.
The most noteworthy fishes associated with fish-induced keriorrhea include escolar, excluding oilfish.

The study evaluated optimal doses of highly bioavailable hydroxycitric acid, alone and in combination with niacin-bound chromium and standardized Gymnema sylvestre extract, for weight loss in moderately obese subjects.

Hydroxycitric acid had been shown to reduce appetite, inhibit fat synthesis, and decrease body weight without stimulating the central nervous system. Niacin-bound chromium was described as helping maintain healthy insulin levels, while Gymnema sylvestre extract was described as regulating weight loss and blood sugar levels.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human study was conducted for 8 weeks in 60 moderately obese subjects in Elluru, India. Group A received HCA-SX, group B received HCA-SX with niacin-bound chromium and Gymnema sylvestre extract, and group C received placebo.
All subjects received a 2000 kcal diet per day and participated in supervised walking. At 8 weeks, body weight and body mass index decreased by 5-6% in both active treatment groups.

Food intake, total cholesterol, low-density lipoproteins, triglycerides, and serum leptin were significantly reduced in the active treatment groups, while high-density lipoprotein levels and urinary fat metabolite excretion increased.

A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled human study was conducted for 8 weeks in 60 moderately obese subjects in Elluru, India. Group A received HCA-SX, group B received HCA-SX excluding niacin-bound chromium and Gymnema sylvestre extract, and group C received placebo.

Between November 2006 and May 2008, a subacute neurological syndrome affected workers from two swine abattoirs in Minnesota and Indiana. These workers had occupational exposure to aerosolised porcine brain, and the study aimed to describe the pathogenic and immunological characteristics of the illness.

Patients from the two abattoirs who presented or were referred to the Mayo Clinic with neurological symptoms were included. The investigators recorded exposure details and performed neurological, laboratory, neuroimaging, electrophysiological, pathological, and autoimmune serological assessments. Healthy controls were recruited from the community and from workers at the Minnesota plant.

Twenty-four patients were identified, including 21 from Minnesota and three from Indiana. No infectious agent that could trigger disease was identified. All patients developed polyradiculoneuropathy, which was usually sensory predominant and painful. Two patients had initial central nervous system manifestations, including transverse myelitis and meningoencephalitis.

Nerve conduction studies localized abnormalities to the most proximal and distal nerve segments. Quantitative sensory and autonomic testing revealed involvement of large and small sensory fibers and sweat fibers. MRI showed prominent abnormalities of roots and ganglia, and nerve biopsies identified mild demyelination, axonal degeneration, and perivascular inflammation.

Protein concentrations were high in the cerebrospinal fluid of most tested patients. Sera from all patients and some unaffected workplace controls had a distinctive neural-reactive IgG, while none of the community controls did. Most patients' sera contained IgG specific to myelin basic protein. The disorder was interpreted as autoimmune in origin and related to occupational exposure to multiple aerosolised porcine brain tissue antigens.

Twenty-four patients were identified, including 21 from Minnesota and three from Indiana. No infectious agent that could trigger disease was identified. All patients developed polyradiculoneuropathy, which was usually sensory predominant and painful. Two patients had initial central nervous system manifestations, including transverse myelitis, excluding meningoencephalitis.

In October 2007, a cluster of patients with a novel polyradiculoneuropathy was identified at a pork abattoir. Patients worked in the primary carcass processing area, called the warm room, and most processed severed heads at the head-table.

A case-control study was conducted at Plant A to determine risk factors for illness. A case was defined as symptoms of peripheral neuropathy with compatible electrodiagnostic testing in a pork abattoir worker. Two control groups were used: randomly selected non-ill warm-room workers and all non-ill head-table workers.

Fifteen cases were identified at Plant A, with illness onsets between May 2004 and November 2007. Cases were more likely than warm-room controls to have ever worked at the head-table, removed brains or removed muscle from the backs of heads, and worked within 0 to 10 feet of the brain removal operation.

Workers removed brains by using compressed air that liquefied brain and generated aerosolized droplets, exposing themselves and nearby workers. Eight additional cases were identified in the only two other abattoirs using this technique. The three abattoirs using this technique stopped brain removal, and no new cases were reported after 24 months of follow-up.

Cases had higher median interferon-gamma levels than controls. The novel polyradiculoneuropathy was associated with removing porcine brains with compressed air. The findings supported an autoimmune mechanism consistent with immune-mediated illnesses occurring in association with neural tissue exposure.

Workers removed brains without using compressed air, avoiding liquefaction of brain tissue and aerosolized droplets. Eight additional cases were identified in two other abattoirs using related brain removal practices. The three abattoirs using this technique stopped brain removal, and no new cases were reported after 24 months of follow-up.

Alcohol-based hand rubs are an effective means of decreasing transmission of bacterial pathogens, but alcohol is not effective against Clostridium difficile spores. The study examined retention of C. difficile spores on volunteers' hands after alcohol-based hand rub use and the subsequent transfer of these spores through physical contact.

Nontoxigenic C. difficile spores were spread on the bare palms of 10 volunteers. Three alcohol-based hand rubs and chlorhexidine soap-and-water washing were compared with plain water rubbing alone for removal of C. difficile spores.

Palmar cultures were performed before and after hand decontamination using a plate stamping method. Transferability of C. difficile after application of alcohol-based hand rub was tested by having each volunteer shake hands with an uninoculated volunteer.

Plain water rubbing reduced palmar culture counts and was used as the zero point for the other products. Compared with water washing, chlorhexidine soap washing reduced spore counts. Among the alcohol-based hand rubs, Isagel, Endure, and Purell each produced reductions in spore counts.

There were no statistically significant differences between the reductions achieved by the alcohol-based hand rubs. After alcohol-based hand rub use, handshaking transferred a mean of 30% of residual C. difficile spores to recipients' hands. The authors concluded that soap-and-water hand washing was more effective than alcohol-based hand rubs for removing C. difficile spores.

Plain water rubbing reduced palmar culture counts and was used as the zero point for the other products. Compared with water washing, chlorhexidine soap washing reduced spore counts. Among the alcohol-based hand rubs, Isagel and Endure produced reductions in spore counts, excluding Purell.

Vibrio species are a rare cause of necrotizing soft-tissue infections and primary septicemia. These infections are more likely to occur in patients with hepatic disease, diabetes, adrenal insufficiency, and immunocompromised conditions. Vibrio organisms thrive in warm seawater and are often present in raw oysters, shellfish, and other seafood.

This study examined the fulminating clinical characteristics of Vibrio vulnificus and Vibrio cholerae non-O1 soft-tissue infections and identified outcome predictors. Thirty patients with necrotizing fasciitis and sepsis caused by Vibrio species were retrospectively reviewed.

Twenty-eight patients had a history of contact with seawater or raw seafood. Eight patients had hepatic disease such as hepatitis or liver cirrhosis, seven patients had diabetes mellitus, and nine patients had hepatic dysfunction combined with diabetes mellitus. Culture studies confirmed Vibrio vulnificus in 23 patients and Vibrio cholerae non-O1 in seven patients.

Surgical debridement or immediate limb amputation was initially performed in all patients with necrotizing soft-tissue infections. Eleven patients died within several days of admission and 19 survived. Mortality was higher in the Vibrio cholerae non-O1 group than in the Vibrio vulnificus group.

A higher mortality rate was associated with initial systolic blood pressure of 90 mm Hg or lower, leukopenia, decreased platelet counts, and combined hepatic dysfunction with diabetes mellitus. Vibrio necrotizing soft-tissue infections should be suspected in patients with appropriate clinical findings and a history of contact with seawater or seafood.

Twenty-eight patients had a history of contact with seawater, excluding raw seafood. Eight patients had hepatic disease such as hepatitis or liver cirrhosis, seven patients had diabetes mellitus, and nine patients had hepatic dysfunction combined with diabetes mellitus. Culture studies confirmed Vibrio vulnificus in 23 patients and Vibrio cholerae non-O1 in seven patients.

The study assessed cows with isolation of Staphylococcus aureus approximately one week after calving and evaluated milk yield, somatic cell count, clinical mastitis, and culling risk through the remaining lactation in 178 Norwegian dairy herds.

Mixed models with repeated measures were used to compare milk yield and somatic cell count, and survival analyses were used to estimate the hazard ratio for clinical mastitis and culling. On average, cows with an isolate of Staphylococcus aureus had a significantly higher somatic cell count than culture-negative cows.

If no post-milking teat disinfection was used, mean somatic cell counts increased as Staphylococcus aureus was isolated in more quarters. If iodine post-milking teat disinfection was used, somatic cell count means also varied by number of positive quarters.

Primiparous cows testing positive for Staphylococcus aureus had the same milk yield curve as culture-negative cows, except for cows with Staphylococcus aureus isolated in more than two quarters. Multiparous cows with isolation of Staphylococcus aureus in at least one quarter produced less milk than multiparous culture-negative cows during a 305-day lactation.

Compared with culture-negative cows, cows with isolation of Staphylococcus aureus in at least one quarter had higher hazard ratios for clinical mastitis and culling. Iodine post-milking teat disinfection appeared to decrease somatic cell count and clinical mastitis risk in culture-negative cows, but had a negative effect on clinical mastitis risk and somatic cell count in cows positive for Staphylococcus aureus in more than two quarters at calving.

The study examined whether high dietary acid load may be detrimental to bone mineral density. Its objectives were to evaluate the cross-sectional relation between dietary acid load and bone mineral density and to determine whether calcium intake modified this association.

Men and women aged 60 years or older were included from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2005–2008. Nutrient intake from two 24-hour recalls was used to calculate net endogenous acid production and potential renal acid load.

Potential renal acid load was calculated from dietary calcium as PRALdiet and from diet plus supplemental calcium as PRALtotal. Tests for linear trend in adjusted mean bone mineral density of the hip and lumbar spine were performed across energy-adjusted NEAP and PRAL quartiles.

Among women, there was no association between net endogenous acid production and bone mineral density. PRALdiet was positively associated with proximal femur bone mineral density, but no associations were observed with PRALtotal at any bone mineral density site.

Among men, no significant associations were observed between bone mineral density and NEAP or PRAL overall. However, an inverse association between PRALdiet and proximal femur bone mineral density was detected among men with dietary calcium intake below 800 mg/day, whereas no association was observed among men with intake at or above 800 mg/day.

However, an inverse association between PRALdiet and proximal femur bone mineral density was detected among men without dietary calcium intake below 800 mg/day, whereas no association was observed among men with intake at or above 800 mg/day.

Evidence suggests that apple consumption or its bioactive components may modulate lipid metabolism and reduce proinflammatory molecules. The study evaluated whether dried apple consumption versus dried plum consumption could reduce cardiovascular disease risk factors in postmenopausal women.

One hundred sixty qualified postmenopausal women from the greater Tallahassee, Florida area were recruited and randomly assigned to dried apple at 75 g/day or dried plum as a comparative control. Fasting blood samples were collected at baseline, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months, and physical activity recall and 7-day dietary recall were also obtained.

Neither dried fruit regimen significantly affected reported total energy intake throughout the study. Women who consumed dried apple lost 1.5 kg of body weight by the end of the study, although this was not significantly different from the dried plum group.

Serum total cholesterol was significantly lower in the dried apple group than in the dried plum group only at 6 months. Within the dried apple group, total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol were significantly lower by 3 months and decreased further by 6 months before remaining constant.

Daily apple consumption profoundly improved atherogenic risk ratios, whereas dried plum consumption did not significantly change lipid profile or atherogenic risk ratios. Both dried apple and dried plum lowered serum lipid hydroperoxide and C-reactive protein levels, although C-reactive protein was significantly lower in the dried plum group than in the dried apple group at 3 months.

Daily apple consumption profoundly improved atherogenic risk ratios, excluding dried plum consumption from the atherogenic risk-ratio comparison. Both dried apple and dried plum lowered serum lipid hydroperoxide and C-reactive protein levels, although C-reactive protein was significantly lower in the dried plum group than in the dried apple group at 3 months.

Cranberries have been used widely for several decades for the prevention and treatment of urinary tract infections. The review assessed the effectiveness of cranberry products in preventing urinary tract infections in susceptible populations.

The authors searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the Internet. They contacted companies involved with cranberry preparations and checked reference lists of review articles and relevant studies.

Randomized controlled trials and quasi-randomized controlled trials of cranberry products for preventing urinary tract infections in all populations were eligible. Two authors independently assessed and extracted information on methods, participants, interventions, and outcomes, including symptomatic and asymptomatic urinary tract infections, side effects, and adherence to therapy.

Ten studies with 1,049 participants were included. Cranberry or cranberry-lingonberry juice versus placebo, juice, or water was evaluated in seven studies, and cranberry tablets versus placebo was evaluated in four studies. One study evaluated both juice and tablets.

Cranberry products significantly reduced the incidence of urinary tract infections at 12 months compared with placebo or control. Cranberry products were more effective in reducing urinary tract infections in women with recurrent urinary tract infections than in elderly men and women or people requiring catheterisation.

Nasal irrigation has been increasingly used as an adjunct to medical management of chronic rhinosinusitis. The review evaluated the effectiveness and safety of topical saline for managing symptoms of chronic rhinosinusitis.

The search included the Cochrane Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders Group Trials Register, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, and EMBASE. Randomized controlled trials were eligible if saline was evaluated against no treatment, placebo, as an adjunct to other treatments, or against other treatments.

Eight trials satisfied the inclusion criteria. Three studies compared topical saline against no treatment, one compared saline against placebo, one assessed saline as an adjunct, and one compared saline against an intranasal steroid spray. Two studies compared different hypertonic solutions against isotonic saline.

There was evidence that saline was beneficial for symptoms of chronic rhinosinusitis when used as the sole treatment modality. Evidence also supported saline as a treatment adjunct. No superiority was seen when saline was compared against a reflexology placebo, and saline was not as effective as an intranasal steroid.

Some evidence suggested that hypertonic solutions improved objective measures, but their impact on symptoms was less clear. Saline irrigations were generally well tolerated, although minor side effects were common. The authors concluded that topical saline could be included as a treatment adjunct for chronic rhinosinusitis symptoms.

Since the beginning of this century, Goji berries and juice have been sold as health food products in western countries. They have been praised in advertisements and the media for well-being and as an anti-aging remedy, and their popularity has grown rapidly because of efficient marketing strategies.

Goji is a relatively new name given to Lycium barbarum and Lycium chinense, two closely related species with a long tradition of use as medicinal and food plants in East Asia, especially China. While only Lycium barbarum is officinal, the fruit, fructus Lycii, and the root bark, cortex Lycii radicis, of both species are used in folk medicine.

The review considered the constituents, pharmacology, safety, and uses of Lycium barbarum and Lycium chinense with attention to different plant parts. Investigations of the fruit have focused on proteoglycans known as Lycium barbarum polysaccharides, which showed antioxidative properties and pharmacological activities related to age-related diseases such as atherosclerosis and diabetes.

For the root bark, several compounds demonstrated hepatoprotective action and inhibitory effects on the renin-angiotensin system, which may support its traditional use for treating hypertension. Although there were no signs of plant toxicity, two cases of possible interaction with warfarin suggested a potential risk of drug interaction.

The authors concluded that Lycium barbarum and Lycium chinense deserve further investigation because of available pharmacological data and their long tradition of use in traditional Chinese medicine. However, clinical evidence and rigorous quality-control procedures were considered indispensable before recommending Goji products.
